number.$description: Choose unitless values by their intended interface role instead of consuming primitive scale steps directly.

opacity.$description: Use opacity roles to communicate interface states consistently.

disabled.$description: Use as the opacity for disabled elements that remain visible but unavailable for interaction.

layer.$description: Choose a stacking level by the relationship it expresses. Popups that use Base UI portals, native popovers, or `<dialog>` are layered automatically; do not give them a layer.

background.$description: Use for decorative content placed behind other content within an isolated component or application stacking context.

raised.$description: Use to lift an element above its siblings within the same stacking context, such as a control overlapping a field or text above a decorative bleed.

floating.$description: Use for panels anchored in the page that scroll with it, such as a compact table of contents opened in place. They stay below sticky page chrome.

sticky.$description: Use for sticky or fixed page chrome that content scrolls under, such as a sticky header or a fixed side navigation.

overlay.$description: Use when a host application needs an explicit overlay layer above its content, such as a skip link. Keep document-ordered portal families, including Base UI nested popups, on a consistent automatic layer instead of assigning this value to individual parts.
